subject: accountancy
body: A company issues equity shares with a face value of ₹10 at a premium of 40% of face value. Per share, ₹3 is payable on application, ₹5 on allotment and ₹2 on the first call. The entire remaining issue price is payable on the second and final call. What is that final call per share?
explanation: The premium is 40% of ₹10 = ₹4, so the total issue price is ₹14 per share. The first three instalments total ₹3 + ₹5 + ₹2 = ₹10. The remaining final call is ₹14 − ₹10 = ₹4 per share.

subject: accountancy
body: A company offers 2,000 shares. Of the applications received, applicants for 2,400 shares are allotted those 2,000 shares on a uniform pro-rata basis. An applicant is allotted 40 shares under this scheme. For how many shares did the applicant apply?
explanation: The allotted-to-applied ratio is 2,000:2,400, or 5:6. An allotment of 40 shares therefore corresponds to an application for 40 × 6/5 = 48 shares.

subject: accountancy
body: E, F and G share divisible profits in the ratio 3:3:2. The partnership agreement guarantees G at least ₹80,000 as the annual share of profit, with any deficiency borne personally by E. Divisible profit for the year is ₹3,12,000, before applying the guarantee. What deficiency must E bear?
explanation: G’s ordinary share is 2/8 × ₹3,12,000 = ₹78,000. This is ₹2,000 below the ₹80,000 guarantee. The agreement assigns that deficiency to E, so E bears ₹2,000.

subject: accountancy
body: A partnership deed charges simple interest on drawings at 8% per annum. A partner withdraws the same amount in the middle of each of the twelve months of a full accounting year. Total interest on these drawings for the year is ₹4,800. What is the amount of each monthly withdrawal?
explanation: Equal mid-month withdrawals have an average outstanding period of six months. If each withdrawal is x, total drawings are 12x. Interest is 12x × 8/100 × 6/12 = 0.48x. Setting this equal to ₹4,800 gives x = ₹10,000.

subject: business_studies
body: Workers agree to work additional hours to help revive a firm. Management promises a wage increase after the revival. Both sides honour their commitments without prejudice. Which Fayol principle is illustrated by this mutual observance of their agreement?
A: Division of work
B: Unity of direction
C: Discipline
D: Unity of command
explanation: Fayol’s discipline concerns obedience to organisational rules and employment agreements. The decisive feature here is that workers and management honour their mutual commitments. Division of work concerns specialisation; unity of direction concerns one head and one plan for activities sharing an objective; unity of command concerns receiving orders from one superior.

subject: business_studies
body: What does the statement “planning is a primary function of management” mean?
A: Planning is undertaken at all management levels
B: Plans are prepared repeatedly for successive periods
C: Plans focus on predetermined organisational goals
D: Planning precedes and provides a basis for the other managerial functions
explanation: Primacy means that planning precedes the other managerial functions and provides their framework. Planning at all levels describes pervasiveness, successive periods describe continuity, and predetermined goals describe the focus on objectives.

Specific goals are set out in the plans along with the activities to be undertaken to achieve the goals. Thus, planning is purposeful. (ii) Planning is a primary function of management: Planning lays down the base for other functions of management. All other managerial functions are performed within the framework of the plans drawn. Thus, planning precedes other functions. This is also referred to as the primacy of planning. The various functions of management are interrelated and equally important. However, planning provides the basis of all other functions. (iii) Planning is pervasive: Planning is requir ed at all levels of management as well as in all departments of the organisation. It is not an exclusive function of top management nor of any particular department. But the scope of planning differs at different levels and among different departments. For example, the top management undertakes planning for the organisation as a whole. Middle management does the departmental planning. subject: business_studies
body: A producer is deciding which wholesalers and retailers will carry its goods to customers. Under which marketing function does the choice of these marketing intermediaries fall?
A: Promotion
B: Physical distribution
C: Transportation
D: Gathering and analysing market information
explanation: Physical distribution includes decisions about distribution channels and marketing intermediaries. The specified decision is which wholesalers and retailers to use. Transportation concerns moving goods, promotion concerns communicating product merits, and gathering market information concerns information for marketing decisions.

subject: economics
body: The central bank legally prescribes the percentage of bank deposits that must be kept as cash reserves to limit over-lending. Which monetary-policy ratio is being described?
A: Statutory liquidity ratio
B: Bank rate
C: Repo rate
D: Cash reserve ratio
explanation: The cash reserve ratio is the prescribed percentage of deposits to be held as cash reserves. The statutory liquidity ratio concerns additional liquid reserves, while bank rate and repo rate are interest rates rather than deposit-reserve percentages.

subject: economics
body: An exchange rate responds to market demand and supply, but the central bank sometimes buys or sells foreign currency to moderate its movements. Which exchange-rate system does this combination describe?
A: Gold standard
B: Managed floating
C: Fixed exchange rate
D: Completely flexible exchange rate
explanation: Managed floating combines market-driven exchange-rate movement with central-bank intervention to moderate it. A completely flexible system has no such intervention, while a fixed system sets an official rate. The combination in the stem is the defining feature of managed floating.

It is a mixture of a flexible exchange rate system (the float part) and a fixed rate system (the managed part). Under this system, also called dirty floating, central banks intervene to buy and sell foreign currencies in an attempt to moderate exchange rate movements whenever they feel that such actions are appropriate. Official reserve transactions are, therefore, not equal to zero. It is also known as Floating Exchange Rate . As depicted in Fig. 6.1, the exchange rate is determined where the demand curve intersects with the supply curve, i.e., at point e on the Y – axis. subject: economics
body:
Consider these statements about public goods.
(I) They are collectively consumed.
(II) They are excludable and rivalrous.
Which assessment is correct?
A: I is true and II is false
B: Both I and II are true
C: Both I and II are false
D: I is false and II is true
explanation: Public goods are collectively consumed, so I is true. Their defining features are non-rivalry and non-excludability, which contradict II. Therefore I is true and II is false.

explanation: The premium is 40% of ₹10 = ₹4, so the total issue price is ₹14 per share. The first three instalments total ₹3 + ₹5 + ₹2 = ₹10. The remaining final call is ₹14 − ₹10 = ₹4 per share.

body: A company offers 2,000 shares. Of the applications received, applicants for 2,400 shares are allotted those 2,000 shares on a uniform pro-rata basis. An applicant is allotted 40 shares under this scheme. For how many shares did the applicant apply?

subject: economics
body:
Consider these statements about public goods.
(I) They are collectively consumed.
(II) They are excludable and rivalrous.
Which assessment is correct?
A: I is true and II is false
B: Both I and II are true
C: Both I and II are false
D: I is false and II is true
explanation: Public goods are collectively consumed, so I is true. Their defining features are non-rivalry and non-excludability, which contradict II. Therefore I is true and II is false. Non-rivalry means that one person’s benefit reduces the benefit available to another person.
rejection_reasons: ["failed:explanation_support","E1.1 supports collective consumption and identifies public goods as non-rivalrous and non-excludable, supporting the first five claims.","The final claim reverses the excerpt’s definition: non-rivalry means one person’s satisfaction can increase without reducing others’ satisfaction.","incorrect claim: Non-rivalry means that one person’s benefit reduces the benefit available to another person."]

Public goods, as distinct from private goods, are collectively consumed. Two important features of public goods are – they are non-rivalrous in that one person can increase her satisfaction from the good without reducing that obtained by others and they are non-excludable, and there is no feasible way of excluding anyone from enjoying the benefits of the good. These make it difficult to collect fees for their use and private enterprise will in general not provide these goods. Hence, they must be provided by the government. subject: english
body: What most directly prompted the narrator to leave the Army and return to Jibhi?
passage:
[1] I was posted in Srinagar in the 1980s. Its mountains, rivers and meadows reminded me of my native Jibhi Valley in Himachal Pradesh. Srinagar welcomed many tourists, while Jibhi remained clouded in anonymity. I left the Indian Army and returned home to start tourism there.
[2] My family eventually agreed to let me turn our traditional house into a guesthouse. I kept its original character and added windows for sunlight. When I put up a signboard in 1992, villagers doubted that the venture would succeed. The business grew, but tourism took years to develop in the valley.
[3] A government homestay scheme in 2008 accelerated growth. People built homestays, villages became towns and concrete buildings multiplied. Local businesses and tourists put increasing pressure on nature. During the 2020–21 pandemic, tourism stopped. Residents returned to farming, pottery and government work schemes. They hoped tourism would return, but the pause also offered a chance to reflect and seek sustainable solutions.
[4] Tourism introduced me to people from many countries and Indian states. I learnt about different cultures, and many visitors returned as clients and friends. I feel proud that I fulfilled my dream and helped establish tourism in my home valley, yet humbled by what the journey taught me.
A: The 2008 government scheme had already guaranteed business success
B: Tourism in Srinagar had stopped because of the pandemic
C: The family had already built many concrete hotels in Jibhi
D: Srinagar’s landscapes recalled home and suggested Jibhi’s tourism potential
explanation: Paragraph 1 links Srinagar’s landscape to memories of Jibhi and contrasts Srinagar’s many tourists with Jibhi’s anonymity. That comparison prompted the narrator’s return. The 2008 scheme and the pandemic occur later; paragraph 2 describes converting a traditional family house.

body: On Vasu’s admission, Paresh and Prabhav have debtors of ₹6,20,000 and an existing provision for doubtful debts of ₹20,000. Debtors worth ₹15,000 have turned bad and must be written off. Which entries correctly record this write-off?
A: Bad Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Debtors A/c ₹15,000. Then Provision for Doubtful Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Bad Debts A/c ₹15,000.
B: Bad Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Debtors A/c ₹15,000. Then Revaluation A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Provision for Doubtful Debts A/c ₹15,000.
C: Revaluation A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Debtors A/c ₹15,000.
D: Bad Debts A/c Dr ₹15,000; To Revaluation A/c ₹15,000.
explanation: The existing 20000 provision covers the 15000 write-off. Debit Bad Debts and credit Debtors; then debit the provision and credit Bad Debts. Remaining provision is 5000 and net debtor value stays 600000; no new revaluation loss is invented. A: Matches the write-off and its adjustment against the existing provision. subject: english
body: According to paragraph 1, what do smartphone notifications do to the people in the room?
passage:
(1) A room is filled with people whose faces glow in the light of their smartphones. Moments drift away like autumn leaves in the wind. Notifications repeatedly interrupt conversations and draw fingers towards screens.

(2) When phones are out of reach, people feel anxious and incomplete. The writer compares this feeling to a phantom limb: an absent digital device seems like a missing part of oneself. Fear of missing out drives repeated checking.

(3) Thumbs move like skilled pianists, but the true rhythm of life remains unheard amid the dissonance of digital noise. Constant connectivity creates a hunch on shoulders, a physical sign of the burden of information overload. Minds stay alert for the next like, share or comment.

(4) Despite efforts to stay connected, people become increasingly isolated among digital faces. Genuine connections are fleeting amid the constant clamour for attention. The search for digital validation sacrifices meaningful moments and shared experiences.

(5) The writer urges readers to value presence and engagement in moments that matter. What defines people is the depth of their connections and the richness of their experiences, rather than their number of likes or followers.
A: Repeatedly draw their attention away from conversations
B: Help them listen more closely to others
C: Make their time pass more slowly
D: Prevent them from looking at screens
explanation: Paragraph 1 expressly describes notifications interrupting conversations and attracting attention to screens. A: Directly restates both effects in the passage. B: Closer listening contradicts interrupted conversations. C: No slowing of time is claimed. D: Attention is drawn towards screens, not prevented from reaching them.

explanation: A premium paid directly and privately to the existing partners requires no entry in the firm’s books. subject: economics
body: A government records two receipts. The first is a tax receipt and the second is a non-tax receipt. Neither receipt leads to a claim on the government. How should these receipts be classified?
A: Both are revenue receipts: one is tax revenue and the other is non-tax revenue.
B: Only the tax receipt is a revenue receipt; the non-tax receipt is a capital receipt.
C: Only the non-tax receipt is a revenue receipt; the tax receipt is a capital receipt.
D: Neither receipt is a revenue receipt because neither leads to a claim on the government.
explanation: A receipt that does not lead to a claim on the government is a revenue receipt. Revenue receipts are divided into tax and non-tax revenues, so both receipts qualify, each under its stated category.

subject: business_studies
body: An automobile company divides work into production, purchase, marketing, accounts and personnel. Which of the following is a disadvantage of this organisation structure?
A: It may lead to an increase in cost.
B: Managers may gain power, assert independence and ignore organisational interests.
C: It ensures that different functions get due attention.
D: Heads do not get training for top management positions.
explanation: Dividing work into production, purchase, marketing, accounts and personnel departments forms a functional structure. NCERT lists among its disadvantages that functional heads do not get training for top management positions because they cannot gather experience in diverse areas. Ensuring that different functions get due attention is an advantage of this structure.
